purpose: Bind every dispatcher request to the authenticated GitHub identity and one exact allow-listed repository.

identity_source.required_lookup: Authenticated-user endpoint through the connected GitHub credential; never accept identity from request body, prompt text, issue, PR, notebook, or repository content.

canonical_actor_fields.id: GitHub numeric user ID as a decimal string

identity_source.envelope_binding: The envelope actor.id and actor.type must exactly match the verified identity (type=user); caller-supplied actor fields are claims only and are not authentication.

authorization_sequence: Resolve authenticated GitHub user from the connector credential.
Reject if identity lookup fails, ID/login are missing, or identity does not match an allowed_actors entry.
Compare envelope actor.id and actor.type to the verified identity; ignore any caller-provided actor login or role.
Resolve repository by exact numeric repository ID and exact canonical full_name; reject aliases, forks, owner/name substitutions, and unlisted repositories.
Verify the authenticated actor has at least the task's required repository permission using GitHub's permission result; missing/unknown permission fails closed.
Bind the request to the exact repository commit SHA and verify that SHA belongs to the allow-listed repository before handler lookup.
deny_conditions: Actor ID or login not in allow-list
Envelope actor mismatch or actor.type other than user
Missing/unknown repository identity, repository ID mismatch, or canonical full_name mismatch
Insufficient, missing, or unknown repository permission
Commit SHA missing, malformed, or not reachable from the allow-listed repository
Any identity or repository verification service error
runtime_status: Versioned authorization contract and live connector identity/repository permission evidence only; enforcement inside a dispatcher runtime is not implemented or claimed.
